question: Should ClawSweeper own an advisory release-train scope-reporting lane, and what explicit PR metadata and maintainer decisions are authoritative for inclusion, exceptions, and incomplete results?
rationale: Existing machinery can carry the reports, but current repository behavior does not define the release policy, ownership boundary, metadata schema, or whether ClawSweeper should govern this part of the release process.

options.title: Sponsor staged advisory lane
options.body: Approve the metadata contract and build read-only audit/reporting first, followed by one shadow release train before any enforcement discussion.

options.title: Consume external release evidence
options.body: Keep release policy in OpenClaw or its release tooling and let ClawSweeper display only authoritative evidence produced there.

options.title: Decline release-governance scope
options.body: Keep ClawSweeper focused on issue, pull-request, repair, and commit maintenance without adding a release-train lane.

recommendation.title: Sponsor staged advisory lane
recommendation.body: Approve the metadata contract and build read-only audit/reporting first, followed by one shadow release train before any enforcement discussion.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available repository-direction candidate for deciding whether this new governance lane fits ClawSweeper’s intended product boundary.
